headline: Pope will not need therapy after cancer surgery — doctors
standfirst: VATICAN CITY, Holy See (AFP) — Pope Leo XIV will not need therapy following an operation last week to remove a cancerous tumour from his lung, his doctors said in a statement released by the Vatican on Wednesday.
body_markdown:
VATICAN CITY, Holy See (AFP) — Pope Leo XIV will not need therapy following an operation last week to remove a cancerous tumour from his lung, his doctors said in a statement released by the Vatican on Wednesday. Test results showed the 71-year-old's cancer "was localised" and "a subsequent oncological assessment confirmed that no further therapy is required", the statement said. Leo, who was only elected last year as the first United States (US) pope, told followers on October 11 that he would be having surgery to remove a nodule. (Jamaica Observer)

**CBS News** adds: Pope Leo won't need further treatment after his surgery for lung cancer, the Vatican announced on Wednesday. CBS News foreign correspondent Chris Livesay reports.

**NBC News** adds: Pope Leo, 71, had received a surgery earlier this month at Rome’s Gemelli Hospital to remove a lung nodule found during recent routine medical tests.

**South China Morning Post** adds: Pope Leo needs no further treatment for lung cancer after follow-up tests confirmed the disease was localised, the Vatican said in a statement on Wednesday. Leo, 71, had the lower lobe of his right lung removed last week in the first major health event of his 17-month pontificate.
